punchline: Sinclair thinks every cell carries a famine-and-cold alarm that a warm, well-fed life rarely sounds.
thirty_sec: Sinclair says cells inherit a survival circuit, sirtuins, mTOR and AMPK, built for famine and cold. Modern comfort keeps it quiet. Mild stress such as a skipped meal, cold or hard exercise switches it on, and sirtuins push cells toward defence and repair. Parts of this rest on animal work, so treat it as his argument.
